utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-98-34-T, the Prosecutor versus Martinovic and Naletilic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness W. I'm just going to caution you again, please, because of the protections that have been granted to you, not to use your name, or names of family names, that sort of information which might identify you. Witness, we left off yesterday afternoon, you were on the bus to Ljubuski. You said at one point the bus stopped, I believe, somewhere around Krcine, and you said that the HVO soldiers fired their guns over your heads. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't think your response came through. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Witness, I was going to ask you - I was asked by Translation, if I can say, yesterday afternoon - if you could speak up and be a bit more clear, it would help us. Did they do anything else? Did the soldiers make you at that point do anything else after the shots were fired? Did some of the prisoners have to do anything else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that moment, there (redacted) (redacted) They were simply taking it out on people in different ways, (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And were several of the prisoners beaten while the bus was stopped at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Among those that you just named, who was particularly or most severely beaten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: My apologies. Can you just say for a moment a bit more about what (redacted) How was he treated, what happened, how did he get back on the bus?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: (redacted) Some water was poured on him. But then when he came to a little, they again beat him thoroughly until a car came to pull out the bus. And when the bus came, they carried – (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And what happened next? You're back on the bus now. What happened next on your way to Ljubuski?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: We came out at Sovicka Vrata, and they stopped the bus and took

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: (redacted) the bus, but he was completely unconscious when he was carried into the bus. And then those guards who had guarded us previously got there, and we used what little water there was on the bus to (redacted), and he came to. And they kept telling us tales on our further way to Ljubuski that they were doing this according to some Dayton Accords, that it was no propaganda and all that. And when we arrived in Ljubuski, they put us in that prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, before you get to Ljubuski itself, you say the bus stopped somewhere near Sovicka Vrata, and was there a changing of the guard around that point, so to speak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have already said that the guards changed and another four boarded the bus, and we set off to Ljubuski.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, help the Chamber, please, so the record is clear. All the things that you have talked about, in terms of the forced singing of songs, the beating, the chewing of bullets, these were all happening during the first set of guards; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the first set, Roba and his team.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Do you know what unit those men, this first set of guards, came from, what HVO unit were they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I know is that Roba was there. And as far as I could see, they were all Tuta's -- rather, Mr. Tuta's soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, is it correct, sir, that you and the others arrived at Ljubuski on about the 19th of April, about 5.00 in the morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: We are not going to spend a great deal of time on your stay at Ljubuski, sir, but is it fair to say --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And I am leading here, Mr. President, just on some background matters about Ljubuski that don't touch on either of the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You were placed there in various cells at a police station. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: There were 10 or 11 cells in what had been, appeared to you, a former horse stables?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some of the policemen were saying that in the former Yugoslavia, it was horse stables, and they were then turned into cells until the new police station was built. And then these were abandoned, but they were put back in use when they had to put us there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And these cells were approximately five or six metres long, and two or three metres wide. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two metres wide and five or six long. There was a passage in front of those cells.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you tell us, please, briefly the name of the warden, if you will, or the person in charge of that prison facility, as far as you knew?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: The one who brought us there and the rest was called Prlic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you possibly spell that name, please, just so we have it accurately in the record, please, if you can?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, the man was called Prlic, P-R-L-I-C.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Now, did you meet another guard while at Ljubuski? And I understand that you do not wish to mention his name, if possible. But did you meet another guard at Ljubuski who provided you some information?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And did he provide you any particular information on things that he had learned about what had happened in Sovici after you left?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I left Sovici -- rather, not only I, when we were expelled from Sovici, and women and children and old, impotent men were expelled, one of the policemen, and I would rather not mention his name, he told me that he was one of the escorts for those of us who had stayed behind in Sovici, to escort them to Gornji Vakuf, and he said that the village had been burned to the ground, that he had escorted women and children over the mountain towards Makljen.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you tell the Chamber whether he said anything to you about some Muslim men being killed near the Sovici school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Once, as I went to the tobacco station for some unloading, he told me that four had been killed in front of a school.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Do you recall the names of these four persons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was Salem Skampo, Hasan Rados, Ekrem Tasic, and Ismet Cilic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm just following the transcript to see how it's coming across.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Some of them are correct, and I won't take the time to ask the witness to spell them. They have come across in the transcript correctly, at least two of them have.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: One man, Hasan, did you say last name Rados, R-a-d-o-s?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And Ismet Cilic, C-i-l-i-c?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, when you were in Ljubuski, did anyone come -- do you recall any occasions when anyone came to take a group of you to do some work or labour?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Men from those units came and took our groups, and we went to fortifications from Popovo Polje to the Buna.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you tell the Chamber whether one of the men who was on the bus that you have named so far in your testimony, did one of those men come to Ljubuski at some point and ask to take a group of you somewhere?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was after the Red Cross registered us. A few days later, Roba came to that prison, made us all come out, and then picked out 17 of us and led us to a bus, (redacted)

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that point, when we were about to board the bus, and then Prlic came out, and he was the commander. And he said that we had been registered by the Red Cross. And when he said that, this one said, So what? Registered? Then he turned his back. And then he said to (redacted), Well, you live after all. Then swore at him and took us back to the prison. And then said, All those who are registered, get inside, and those who had not been registered, stand up.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Let me follow up, please, a couple of points there. You said again, this person, Roba, is this the same Roba or Robo that you have mentioned, for instance, who was on the bus on the way to Ljubuski?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, up to Sovicka Vrata. Yes, Roba was there until we reached Sovicka Vrata.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You said a few days before this, the Red Cross had come to register you. Would you just explain that more to the Chamber, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the Red Cross registered us, we were all issued with those cards, and I have enclosed it. And as of then, we were under some kind of protection.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If you can -- if you understand why, or if you have some idea and can assist the Chamber in this way, can you explain to the Chamber why it would have been significant to Robo, or anyone else, perhaps, in that situation, whether you had already been registered or not registered. What difference would that make?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. But when Prlic mentioned that we had been registered, he just paused and said, Oh, they have been registered, and he made us get off that bus again. And I just don't understand why he wanted to say that in that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You told us a moment ago that in your place, then others were taken who had not been registered?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those people who were taken away had been brought from Mostar a couple of days after our registration, and then he selected 17 men from that group. And I never saw them return either to Ljubuski or to Heliodrom where I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If I can have the usher's assistance, please, I would like to distribute to the courtroom and to the witness Exhibits P879, 880, and 881, which I will say now, I will not put on the ELMO -- ask not to be put on the ELMO. They will have to be under seal because they include the witness's name.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So, Witness, I'm going to caution you. When I put to you this document, don't say anything about your name, or these documents. Now, Witness, I want to direct your attention, first of all, to 879. And again without using your name, will you just simply tell the Chamber what that is? Just tell them what it is.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's this card of the Red Cross, which registered us a week after we arrived in Ljubuski.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. And without saying it again, this card bears your name and gives some information, for instance, about Sovici; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is my identity card under which I was registered, and the place of my birth and the municipality in which it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can I direct your attention, please, to Exhibit 880, which should be the next document. And can you please again tell us what that is, as best you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was given this paper after I came out of the camp. It was a kind of certificate which I needed to get this last document I got from the Red Cross in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And when you said "this last document", is that Exhibit P881, the next document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Is it correct, sir, then, if we look at 881, would you agree with this information - I'm not going to go through all of it in detail - but this would indicate in fact you were registered sometime around the 30th of April, 1993, and you were ultimately released on the 1st of March, 1994; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: The date is correct when I was registered, and the date when we came out of the camp is also correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Now, just tying this back in to your testimony just now a moment, when you told us a few minutes ago that you had been registered by the Red Cross a few days before Robo came, your registration, that is the registration that is reflected in P879; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Now, moving forward, were you taken to some other locations, a line against the Serbs, to do labour there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Ljubuski, we went from Popovo Polje to the Buna. I practically worked all along the front line. I don't think you can find a single part of that front line where I didn't work and build fortifications.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, do you recall whether during that time you were abused or maltreated by any HVO soldiers from Ljubuski or Grude?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was people from Ljubuski and Grude who ill-treated us worst on the front lines. As soon as we came back to the camp, that is, the prison, we let Prlic know, and he immediately stopped giving them people.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, how is it that Prlic had the ability or authority to stop these men from taking you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every morning, Prlic went to the front line where we were to work and, to each one of those who escorted us, said, "Well, if you don't behave intelligently, then you will not get any one of those men. I won't give you any men to work for you until you begin to behave wisely."

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Witness W, you were in a war and Prlic was your warden. But can you tell the Chamber, did he treat you fairly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, as far as I saw him, he treated me correctly, very correctly. And at times he even saved me or, rather, wouldn't let some of those who would ill-treat me take me along, and I think he stopped those men.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, while you were staying in Ljubuski, did you have an altercation with someone as you were moving around outside of the prison one day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: One day, I set out to buy some cigarettes and coffee across the street from the prison. I didn't look around much, I just crossed the road. I went to one of the cafes. One was owned by a Muslim and one was owned by a Croat. On my way back, Tuta noticed me. I was wearing a camouflage uniform, and he shouted at me and told me to come to him. And then at that moment, both owners of the cafes came to Tuta, and one of them, who was Croat by nationality, went out and came to him and waved to me to go away, and they remained with him, quarrelling. And that was the first time I had seen Tuta.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: When you say that Tuta noticed you and "he shouted at me," referring to your testimony just now, do you remember anything in particular that he said to you, any words that he used?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: When he called me, "Balija, come here, fuck your mother," and he says, "What are you doing here," I stood, I looked at him. And when the two owners jumped towards him and came to him, one of them showed me -- signalled me to go away and the other two remained quarrelling. I crossed the road and returned to the prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did you hear either of the two cafe owners say anything to Tuta?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of them was saying, "What are you doing? It's not the way we work here." And then I crossed the road and I was no longer in the hearing distance, as it were.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, this man that you saw that had this altercation that day and you've just described to us, did you see this person some other time, either live, or on a photograph, or TV; did you see this person again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, until I left the camp. Then I saw him on television.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And do you recall the circumstances in which you saw him on television, and can you tell the Chamber whether you could recognise this person as the same man?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I saw him, he was wearing a black uniform with a cap on his head. And when I looked at him, I was very scared. When I saw him on television, I saw him wearing civilian clothes, and he looked the same as when I saw him the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did anyone around this time identify to you -- you've so far only said the word or name "Tuta." Did anyone tell you another name? And if you can remember that, can you tell the Chamber, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the next day when I went to the cafe again, someone told me there -- said that this had been Mladen Naletilic, Tuta. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, is it correct, sir, that after you had been at Ljubuski for about two months, you were taken to the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And can you just describe to the Chamber, if you will briefly, how you came to be transferred to the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the first group that went and said that they were being exchanged, about five or ten days while I was still there, a bus came, collected us. We didn't know where we were going. At that moment when I saw -- when we came to Mostar, to the Heliodrom, I looked and I saw that those that had gone previously did not go to be exchanged but were there at the Heliodrom.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you tell us, then, once you arrived at Heliodrom, who was the person in charge, if you remember, of at least that portion or that building that you were held in.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in that building, the commander was Ante Smiljanic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Is that -- if I can assist, is that S-m-i-l-j-a-n-i-c?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Smiljanic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Now, during the time that you were held at the Heliodrom -- and could I ask you, were you then held continuously at the Heliodrom until you were released on about the 1st of March, 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, from the Heliodrom, we went to different places to dig trenches and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: But then at various times, after those projects, if you will, you would be taken back to the Heliodrom from time to time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, sometimes we would stay away 5, 10, 15 days. Sometimes we would come back every evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: During the time you were there, were there particular guards -- excuse me -- who you remember as treating the prisoners particularly poorly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were some who were really singled out. Miro Marjanovic and Ante Buhovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I can assist, Marjanovic is M-a-r-j-a-n-o-v-i-c. Buhovac is B-u-h-o-v-a-c.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And were you, yourself, your brothers or those close to you included among those that these two men beat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was beaten a few times by Miro Marjanovic and Ante Buhovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Would you just tell the Chamber how this typically would happen, if there was a pattern, or how would these beatings occur?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, once when I was distributing food, something was wrong as far as they were concerned. And then I was slapped in the face a few times and kicked in the back. This was done by Miro Marjanovic, because I failed to say who was the person who was distributing the bread. And Buhovac, once or twice, he came tired -- there was a person coming. He was tired. He fell asleep. And actually, he would beat me because I did not respond to his entrance.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did an HVO soldier that you knew from Sovici appear at the Heliodrom for some time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was some Jozo from the police in Sovici. He spent a few days there. And he beat up Ovnovic and Cilic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: When you say "Jozo," do you remember his last name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pole.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned already that while you were at the Heliodrom, you were taken at various times to do labour on various projects in the region. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Now, I'm not going to take you through all of those, partly because of time. But did you at some time work for a unit called the Benko Penavic unit?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you recall approximately how long you stayed and worked at that location before returning to the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we spent 15 days there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And can you tell the Chamber in general, not just on that occasion but when you were out doing forced labour, was it considered -- and you can explain this in a moment -- was it considered to be, by the prisoners, an advantage to be in civilian clothes or in military uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we were better off wearing civilian clothes because the B and H army, when they saw us, they wouldn't shoot at us.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Were you ever made to put on a uniform and go out in front of the HVO lines?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did you know of other soldiers who were required -- prisoners who were required to do that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I'm not quite sure. I wasn't one of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Now, after the time you worked at the Benko Penavic unit, did you go to -- sometime shortly thereafter, to another location, to another unit in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: After a few days, we went to Stela's for a day or two.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And what did you do there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there, we worked -- we put bags on the windows at the Red Cross in Mostar so as to protect the building. We collected broken glass in front of the windows on the surrounding premises, and when we were -- because the glass would serve as some kind of clue.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Well, let me stop you on a couple of those things. In your testimony just now, at least in the transcript, it came that you said you put bags on the windows of the Red Cross. Were you working at a Red Cross in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first aid -- the first aid unit of the hospital, emergency unit, let's say.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you say the name -- perhaps, in your own language -- can you say the name of that location, what that was called, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Where was this hospital located approximately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: In front of the department store "Hit," in the direction of the Hasana Brkica bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Do you recall any of the streets that this building was located on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the Bulevar, before you -- turning into the Bulevar, it was the Lijeska Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm going to ask the usher to show you, please, Exhibit 14.5. Witness, will you look at Exhibit 14.5, please. Can you tell us, by looking at that photograph, if you recognise the location where you said that you went in your testimony to Stela's for a day or two?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. And you've indicated a building, a kind of semicircular pink building on an intersection, kind of a v-shaped intersection in the middle of the photograph between two streets coming together at an intersection to the -- roughly to the left side. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Seric.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I object to this question of the Prosecution's because the Prosecutor is testifying and not the witness. It is up to the witness to testify.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Forgive me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Maybe you are jumping too fast.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Again, my apology. Maybe it was my mistake. If it is, I do apologise. I thought I saw the witness point, make a circle around those buildings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Can you ask the witness to use a pencil or something to circle that place.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Witness, I'm going to ask the usher to assist you, please, if he can provide you a marker. You made a circle a moment ago with the pointer. Would you make the same circle, if you will, or make the markings on the location you've pointed out. Now, before we come back to that building, we can leave that for a moment on the ELMO. But before we come back to that building, did you stay overnight while you were working for Stela at this -- at that time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Just a minute. Yes, Mr. Seric.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to object because it is suggestive in respect of the time it was to happen. Let the witness tell his own story.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness just testified a moment ago that he stayed a day or two at Stela's. That's what he testified. The next question, I'm just asking, where did you stay while working at Stela's?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is not right. He said during the night. The Prosecutor mentioned the night, and the witness never mentioned the night.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Seric, if the witness said he stayed a day or two at Stela's, it might be that the witness stayed overnight at his place. Maybe the Prosecutor could clear it up.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour, if we have to do it this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, did you work at Stela's more than one day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we worked there for two days --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Stop, stop. Did you go back to the Heliodrom on the night between the two days, or where did you stay on the night between the two days that you worked at Stela's?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we spent the night in -- at Stela's headquarters, in his command in the cellar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Now, I'm going to come back to that again in a moment. Taking you back to the Health Centre, the place that you marked on Exhibit 14.5, can you tell us about an occasion during those two days when you saw two men beaten? Just tell us what happened.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the morning, we came early. When we came on that morning, we were brought there, we cleaned up around the buildings, we cleaned the rooms, we brought the bags. And when we came -- before we left -- before we started working there, two people came and brought another two persons who were apparently hiding. One of them was -- I didn't know either of them and I didn't see them later on. The commander, who was wearing a black camouflage uniform, came to that person and asked him a few questions. First he started hitting that person with his hands, and then he asked for something. And then he -- when his hand started hurting him, then he hit him -- the other one started hitting the one that was watching us, and he said -- he threw away his rifle and he said, "You should kill him and not make him suffer that much."

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Well, Witness, you've told us several things there. These two men were captured. Who was beating them, if you can describe -- you said someone beat them, and can you describe this person a bit more, whatever information you can provide?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said that it was Stela's commander, who was wearing a black camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. And then you said, "The one started hitting the one that was watching us." And, I'm sorry, that's not very clear. Can you tell us more what you mean by that? What happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were two Muslims hiding around those buildings. One of them was an alpinist, and the other one, I don't know what he was. He said that he was the greatest alpinist. And the one who wasn't the alpinist, he was also being beaten.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I think when you're saying "alpinist," this is someone who was saying he was a mountain climber; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: What I'm trying to understand, sir - and my question probably wasn't clear - you said somebody intervened and said something about, essentially, "Just kill him." Who said that and, again, what was said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: The one that was guarding us to avoid us escaping, he made us go to the ground and then he threw his rifle. "You better kill him than make him suffer that much."

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Who was that person addressing, as you understood it, when he said those things?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: He addressed the commander wearing the black camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Now, later that same day, did you see these two prisoners again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were with us. They spent the night with us at the command down. Then we were called again in the morning. We had to clean the garbage, take it away, and this we did until the evening. In the evening, we were taken to Stela's headquarters, and there we were lined up. And then I saw Stela, who came very near us. There was Prlic, who used to -- who knew Stela, who said personally he was in prison before the war. Then I heard that it was Stela. Later on, when the person in the black uniform came up, he said, "We found the two of them because they were hiding." And then Stela came like a boxer coming to a person. He beat him up. He fell down. Then Hasim came, and then they moved away and they were talking about something.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Now, I'll stop you there for a moment, please. You said, "Stela came up to the person and beat him up." When you say "beat him up," "him" being who?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the one that was beaten up was the person that they had found, not the mountain climber. The other one was being beaten up by the person in the black uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And what was Stela doing during that time? I just want to be clear now, because you said a couple of things.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No translation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I didn't get any translation.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can you repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sorry, I'm not getting any translation.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Speak up.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can hear.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I couldn't hear the witness. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You've said a number of things. I want to make sure there isn't confusion in the record. What was Stela doing at that time during what you've just told us about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we came there, the man in black lined us up and he -- someone said that, "We had found two of them." The other person that was not the mountain climber was beaten by the person in the black uniform, and then he was approached and was -- actually, he came to him like a boxer and hit him, and he fell to the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. And, I'm sorry, the "he" that approached him like a boxer, who was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was Stela.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, did you go back to the Heliodrom after that day or after this event?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: About half an hour later, they collected us and took us to the Heliodrom.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And these two men that you've told us about, were they taken back to the Heliodrom with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Witness, in closing, I'm going to show you three photographs. And with the usher's assistance, I would like you to be shown and placed on the ELMO, please, 15.2, 15.9 and 15.37. You can first put on the ELMO 15.2.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you look at that, Witness, and tell us, is there anything on that photograph you recognise?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And what do you see that you recognise?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: When they brought us to a place where we were then lined up against the wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you see the wall where you were lined up at the time these two men were also -- were beaten, as you told us about a moment ago? Can you point that out? Perhaps again if you have the pointer, can you see the wall where you were lined up, where those events happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right here, where I have it now, that is where that wall was against which we were lined up.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And I'm going to ask the usher, please, to provide you a marker.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And if you can just mark that for the record, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm next going to ask you to look at 15.9. Can you tell us if you recognise that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the cellar where we spent that one night.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And I'm showing you 15.37. Do you recognise that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the entrance into the cellar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness W. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Cross-examination. Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Witness. I'm counsel for Mr. Mladen Naletilic and will ask you some questions. Please listen carefully to Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. what I'm asking you, and I will phrase them in a way so as to move on as quickly as possible. And thank you for your understanding. Let me start in this way: Will you please be so kind as to tell me the name of the coffee bar in Ljubuski where you saw -- where you allegedly saw Tuta?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Both those coffee shops were across the street from the prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: But will you please be so kind, because we do not know. Witness, we do not know, and the Honourable Judges do not know where that is. So could you please describe to us where was the prison, the street, and where were those coffee shops?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know where prison is. I never looked at the street because I was only in passing there. I never looked up to see what this coffee shop was called. And opposite the prison were two coffee shops. There was only a street between them and the prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Will you please be so kind as to describe these coffee shops? Did they have terraces, what did they look like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both these coffee shops had terraces.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Do you remember what kind of chairs were there, wooden, metal, or what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I'm asking you this because the Defence has to check that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: But it was eight or nine years ago after all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And because of these eight or nine years, do you remember how many statements you gave to the SDB sector, that is the state security sector, the secret police, its office in Konjic, and how many statements you gave to the gentleman from the OTP?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only two from the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Ah-ha. Do you remember all your statements?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was a long time ago, but yes, more or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Do you know that in the first statement about what happened Ljubuski is not mentioned at all in the first statement that you gave to the secret police in Konjic. In your second statement on the 30th of April, '97, you describe it as follows: I could see that his hair beneath the cap was grey. He wasn't particularly tall, more or less like myself, 174 centimetres, and he had no beard.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry. I'm sorry. I get carried away. I simply get carried away by my heart.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Just one thing, you're speaking so fast and in such a tone that it sounds like an interrogation rather than a cross-examination. So please, please try.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My sincere apology. I simply get carried away. I get carried away. I'll do my best to slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Let me repeat then. In the statement you gave to the investigators, you describe it as follows: An older man wearing a black uniform with a number of insignia on it and a baseball cap with the insignia. I could see that beneath the cap, his hair was grey. He wasn't particularly tall, perhaps my height, 174 centimetres. And he did not have a beard. Wait, wait, wait, I haven't finished.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, I apologise for interrupting. If there's going to be this extensive examination of the witness about the document, it's only fair that the document be marked and put in front of the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Do you have that document at your hands, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, unfortunately, I only have my copy. But the witness said that he remembered, and I am just asking him if he remembers because this is a statement that he signed. I do not see why I should show every single statement to a witness. I really do not understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The question is not that. It is that if you quote a long paragraph from that statement, I think you should show the copy to all the parties, as well as the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, to answer the question, it's ultimately the Chamber's responsibility, of course, and I understand that. But to answer Mr. Krsnik's question about if he has to show the statement to every witness --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Will you slow down, Mr. Scott, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Our position would be yes, he does. If the examination is going to be conducted properly, and there's going to be extensive cross-examination of a witness about a document, the proper procedure is that every witness be provided the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I will ask my colleagues to give me another copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, can you ask the question piece by piece rather than quoting the whole document?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is an exception because in another statement, he gave another description which is opposite to what he said here. That is why I am quoting it. This is an exception. Of course, I will do that going part by part, but already I hear this objection from the Prosecution. And now I have to admit to the Court that I do not have a translation of this document. I cannot give the document to everybody because I do not have enough copies, and that is why I opted for this form of examination, part by part. But this description is very specific, because you find another description in a different statement, and it is quite contrary to what we hear in this one.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Will Mr. Krsnik please slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, not to delay these proceedings, because we are anxious to finish the next witness today, but the Chamber at the first week of trial set out very specific procedures about how documents should be used with witnesses in Court. I thought the instructions were rather clear. The Prosecution has taken steps to comply with the Chamber's orders, and I think Mr. Krsnik can do the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik. That's right. The Chamber has made a decision on presenting of documents on these issues. You could ask the question one by one rather than quoting the whole document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours. I will go by this. And I would like to thank my learned friends for their warning. I'll do my best.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Will you please be so kind. I have just read this out to you. Do you remember making that statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: I gave a statement, but it wasn't read out to me. Perhaps they did not write correctly what I had told them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: What does this mean? You did not read it; you just signed it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't read out to me because I was in a hurry when we were giving that statement. It was very late, and that is why I had no time to read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Now, if I am getting your meaning correctly, are you telling us that somebody brought a written statement to you, and you merely signed it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, perhaps as I was talking, they simply noted it down in a different way. It's not that somebody brought me a ready-made text and that I signed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I must admit that I simply am at a loss at what you are trying to tell me. Will you please explain it to me. Did you say this or didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did, but how did I say that? In my last statement, I have what I said in all of them, but perhaps my words were incorrectly noted down.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: But how could that happen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because it was already late in the afternoon. There wasn't much time, and that is why we did it the way we did it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So -- you did it so that everything is incorrectly recorded; that is, what you said is not in this transcript?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that is the likeliest explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Then, will you tell me so that we can finish with this protocol, your signature, you signed something, and you don't know what you signed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my first statement, yes, I did that accidentally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You have to be very careful with your question. You speak really fast, and one question after another. The interpreter is really behind you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, will you also tell the witness, who immediately answers without leaving enough time for interpreters, to finish with the interpretation of the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Witness, in front of you, there's a monitor, and every word we say in this courtroom will be typed out on the screen. Would you please look at this screen to see the typing is finished. Then you begin to answer the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. President, with your permission, can I say something to Mr. Krsnik. I'm taking a note and following the screen; and frankly, I'm lost. The last time I'm sure that I followed the questioning was when you asked the witness had he made two statements to the OTP. And then you started quoting a statement and mentioning the secret police, I think. And I'm lost. Are you quoting, or were you quoting, from a statement that was made to the offices of the OTP, or are you talking about another statement? It's not clear to me what statement you're actually putting to this witness, which you are, I think, going to compare with another statement. Could you go back a little bit on that, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, thank you for the warning. I realise now that I had done something to my detriment. I made a clear distinction between the record which was done in the secret police. When I read this record, I said it was dated 30th of April, '97. I asked the witness if he remembered it. I opened that statement. I read out to him this part of that. There was an objection. And discussion started. The witness said that in this statement -- that this statement did not reflect correctly his words because he had not read that statement and, instead, merely signed it. They were in a hurry when he was making this statement, and that it had been recorded incorrectly. We heard it all in the courtroom, and I've just repeated it. This is where we are now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I think we are at cross-purposes, Mr. Krsnik. Because even after your explanation, when the witness is talking about a statement that was made in the afternoon and in a hurry, is he talking about a statement to the secret police or to the OTP?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To the OTP. The OTP, because I warned him and I told him that we were talking about that statement. I told the witness that. We are talking about that statement only. Because we decided that the one which was given to the secret police, there is absolutely no mention of it. He does not mention this incident at all. So there is no need to discuss that statement which he gave to the secret police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: So are we talking at this stage about a statement made on the 30th of April, 1997, just so we're clear, because I thought you were talking about a statement to the secret police. You're abandoning that for the moment. I'm clear now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour. You have helped me a great deal.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Now, truly I'm asking you, Witness -- I will do my best to be as slow as possible. You also have to wait after you hear my question, and then you will slow me down, because you can see what kind of misunderstandings can arise if we're too fast. Witness, now let us repeat for the record: This statement that you gave to the OTP that we've just been discussing, you said that things had been recorded incorrectly there; is that it?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness nods.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So what the statement says is not correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, most of the things said there are not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And you nevertheless, without checking it, signed it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Wait, wait. You have to wait for the witness to answer the question "yes" or "no," because it's important.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I am sorry, truly, but this is exactly -- this illustrates the problem. Even after my previous interventions, the statement is still not being put in front of this witness. So now there's a -- he has no statement. There's a ten-page statement. The question was -- there were comments, "So most of the things said there are not correct." Does that mean the whole ten pages are not correct? What statement is he referring to, what part of the statement? The witness should have the statement in front of him, and that's only fair.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We also believe that's fair. You may ask other questions. And during the break, could you make some copies?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very well, Witness. We shall then come back to -- go back to your village of Sovici and leave aside this particular part. You were born in Sovici, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You are familiar with the geography of your birth place and surrounding mountains?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Now, will you please be so kind as to explain to Their Honours, because they have never been there, to try to tell them where is Sovici? Is it in a valley and there are around hills? Can you paint a picture of Sovici, because I will have some questions, so will you please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sovici is 18 kilometres from Jablanica. It is surrounded by hills; that is, with the exception of the direction to Jablanica, it is surrounded by mountains. So there is a road to Sovicka Vrata, and Sovici is in a valley, in a mountain valley.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes, yes, go on.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a rather broad village. That is, one part of Sovici -- Sovici is quite a scattered village, a disbursed village, you know, many houses and hamlets, so that at times there is a 10- or 15-minute walk distance between individual houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And there's only one road in Sovici, from Sovicka Vrata to Jablanica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are two roads.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And which is the second one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: One is the old road through Kraji, called "Kraji," and the another one was built recently. That is, another road was built through Sovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And the old road, was it linked with the Road of Salvation; is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Now, will you tell Their Honours, why was this road called "Road of Salvation," and where is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Road of Salvation was built in the very early days of the war, and it was called the "Road of Salvation" because the bridge towards Mostar had been blown up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And the refugees, as a result of the Serb aggression - and they were mostly Muslim -- that is, Croat refugees - they used that road to save their lives, crossing into Herzegovina and then on to Croatia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, and that road was built by the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And that road was built by the HVO; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was -- well, the construction began before the HVO. The HVO simply made it wider.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And that road links up with that one and only road at Sovicka Vrata; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is not. They link up at Obruc.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Obruc, I see. And it is beneath Sovicka Vrata?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: When somebody is in Sovici, will you explain to Their Honours, where can one get out of the village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: In what direction do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Well, you tell us. Is that correct, that there is an exit to Jablanica and another one to Sovicka Vrata, and that's it by road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you can take a road to come out to Jablanica and another one to Sovicka Vrata. And during the war, there was a road going via Pomen to Gracac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: To Gracac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Could cars take that road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That road was used through -- across Pomen to Gracac, that road was used to travel from Prozor to Sovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You mean the BH army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: From Prozor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Prozor to Gracac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I see, very well. And if you place a checkpoint at the exit towards Jablanica and another checkpoint at Obruc or Sovicka Vrata, then Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. one needs to cross mountains; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And the BH army manned the checkpoint towards Jablanica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Now, tell me, on the 15th of April, why weren't the Croats allowed to enter Jablanica and were stopped at that checkpoint? People -- Matan Zaric was stopped there - he was the president of the HVO and then a councilman in Jablanica - and a Mr. Rogic. Who intercepted them and would not let them proceed to Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know who intercepted them or where. I do not know that. But it is because of the checkpoint which was at Bijeli Potok. At that Bijeli Potok, nobody could go through Bijeli Potok.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Bijeli Potok, you say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And that was manned by the BH army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, by the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So where was the AbiH checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only checkpoint of the BH army was in Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You mean Jablanica itself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the entrance into Jablanica, right next to the entrance into Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: But Jablanica and Doljani is practically one place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but there is 18 kilometres difference between them. No, not 18; 12 kilometres. There's 12 kilometres between them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Twelve kilometres. You mean from the centre of the village of Doljani and the centre of Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the checkpoint to the former centre in Doljani.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I see it is 11.00, so perhaps this would be a convenient time for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, this witness is a material witness for you because he testified that he personally saw your client at a certain point. I hope your questions will be more direct to that particular event. Thank you. We'll adjourn until 11.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Please continue, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, thank you. I simply wanted to tell you that we were not able to make the necessary copies during the break. There were other people making copies. We have three teams in one Defence room, so I shall try to address questions to the witness. We were not able to make the copies in this half hour we had. Your Honours, I simply wanted to say that the counsel believes that we have to deal with Sovici, because this figures in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, let us finish with Doljani and Jablanica. If we take the hamlets and the other settlements, Marica Kuce, and so forth, we can say that they were sort of joint -- linked up to Doljani -- to Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, to some extent, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: That is all I wanted to say, just to give the Chamber an idea. Please tell me, when was the so-called TO set up and who did it comprise in Sovici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Sovici, I don't know the date. It was quite a long time ago. The TO was established with covering the Muslims and Croats in Sovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Could you please tell me how many Croats there were and how many Muslims.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact number. Quite truthfully, I do not know. There were many of both there with the commander of the Muslims, Dzemo Ovnovic. At the head of the HVO of the Croats was Stipo Kopilas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: How many Muslims and how many Croats lived in Sovici? Since you spent your whole lifetime there, I suppose you should know.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the exact number, I cannot say in a few homes. Well, there were about 200 houses, and there were about 50 to 70 Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You mean Croatian houses? Is it a fair statement to say that there were three times more Muslim houses than Croat houses in Sovici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were less Croats, but if we count Doljani --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Please, answer my questions. Now we are discussing Sovici, and then we will discuss Doljani. Was the same situation in the army, three times more Muslims than Croats?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Croats received fresh forces from Herzegovina who were stationed at Risovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You are speaking about 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Why did they need stronger forces in 1992? Didn't we have the same enemy?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. It was not clear to me then.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: How far is Risovac from Sovici, or better, Donja Makljen, which is the centre of Sovici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Doljani by road, by macadam road, about half an hour away.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: By car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, by car.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: In the village, it was the same situation, three to one in the village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the forces were not the same because all those from Donja Jablanica, Jablanica Slatina, they were all stationed at Sovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, did you dig trenches, bunkers, in the surrounding hills, the hills that surround Sovici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Thank you. Against which enemy did you build fortifications?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we were making fortifications, it was against the so-called former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you tell me how far was the nearest soldier of the former JNA, how many kilometres from you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not clear --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me, what time period are we talking about now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Maybe you could clear it up, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, well, I said -- we were talking about 1992, because we are discussing the TO.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I wonder what the relevance of this is, Your Honour. We have serious time constraints today. We are now talking about two lines in 1992, which are not at issue in this witness's testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, is that relevant to the issue?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it is extremely relevant to the issue, and I would ask my learned friend - and he knows what I'm talking about - that he should not speak in the course of my cross in this way, because it is relevant, and he should listen and he will see. Establishing a line between -- vis-a-vis a non-existent enemy was highly -- was only to be expected that they were preparing for an attack.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, you may proceed. But bear in mind that we have very limited time, and I hope you could come to the specific instance in a few minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, very sincerely, I feel very uncomfortable. I believe that this piece of testimony is very relevant. I'm always being time-pressured. I apologise, Your Honour. I know that we have a job to do. But from one witness to another, it depends how fast we can proceed. It is not my fault that examination-in-chief lasted two and a half hours, and now I'm required to finish the cross in 15 minutes' time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No, no, no. Nobody asked you to finish your cross-examination in 15 minutes. We just want you to be more concentrated and to the point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I am concentrating to the maximum. I am doing it for your benefit. You've never been to Sovici, so I want to get the picture. I must ask questions which will lead up to a crucial issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Please tell me when the B and H army was formed.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact date when it was formed. But during the distribution of weapons, the HVO soldiers separated, and they began to build fortifications above our houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: When were weapons distributed to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the date. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Was it in '92 or '93?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: '92, towards the end of '92.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And it was already then that the Croats were fortifying their positions above your homes. Where was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was around the Muslim homes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: How long is the village of Sovici? What is the length of the village of Sovici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Sovici is Sovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: What is the length?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 15 to 20 minutes by car in one direction, so several kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And the Muslim houses are scattered around hamlets, and they managed to encircle all of you in all the hamlets?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, with their -- with new forces coming from other locations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very well. Can you tell me where the AbiH army kept its positions? Were you at Pasje Stijene?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Were you in Obruc?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Were you -- Pasje Stijene to Mackovica was a quote of 9.2. Were those your lines?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only two ditches, two trenches.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So you were higher above their trenches?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Borovnik was higher than Mackovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: We have to go more slowly with the names you are mentioning. Mackovica and Borovnik are at an altitude higher than the village; is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You said that the Croats had encircled you in the village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first circle was around the village, and the second circle was encircling hills with new forces from Eastern Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Eastern Herzegovina. Now, tell me, did you have any assistance in manpower? Your army, did it have any assistance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So no one came from Jablanica, Prozor; people would not come to join the AbiH army in Sovici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Now, please tell me, when was your village attacked, as you say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, our village was attacked in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: The date, please. I'm interested in the date.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that this was the 16th. The 15th, 16th - I don't know the exact date - in the morning, 8.00 or 9.00, I think it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: In all of your three statements and today also, you said that it started on the 16th in the morning, and this is what you maintain now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Now, tell me, did the B and H army have any liaison facilities in Sovici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we had a Motorola, which we established communication with the Jablanica once a day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You said there were 100 or 120 armed soldiers; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And all of you were armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not all of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Who wasn't -- how many of you were not armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, more than half of us had rifles.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did you have heavy weaponry like, for example, PAMs or mortars?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had two mortars, and the two mortars were not used at all, and one PAM.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And one PAM. As far as heavy machine-guns?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was one. We had one 7.9, and that is all, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: When the B and H army and the HVO separated, when did that happen definitely?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Was the commander --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Still a private session, please, just for one question or two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We will go into the private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We are now in the open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you remember your recent statement on November 28th, 2000?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So wrong things went into the statement, or you did not read it Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. and sign it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: I read it. It was translated to me, and I read it and I signed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: There you say that 5.00, you were arrested, along with another 75 men, and all of those arrested were members of the TO. You said that your wife was with the baby at home and not that you were with her?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that day when I was with my wife drinking coffee in the morning, that night, I spent in the school building. And next morning, I went to buy something for breakfast. I returned to the school, and then my wife, and mother with small baby --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Well, I didn't ask you that. And you didn't answer my question. I asked you kindly, you said that you had read your statement and signed your statement. There, it is said that you were --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President. If the Defence, for some reason, can't seem to provide the witness with this statement, we have an extra copy of the statement. We would ask that it be provided to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, permitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: We continue to object to examination in this manner.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The number for this document is D1/18.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, it is on the first page. Just turn the page. It is the tenth paragraph. "About 5.00, I was arrested. All of those who were arrested were members of the TO." Have you read this? "During the attack, my wife and the 50-days-old baby stayed in the house." And so on. "My wife was later taken with all the other women and children -- "

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Counsel, slow down, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] " -- with other women and children to Krcine. She never told me that anything bad happened to them." So the first question, were you actually in the house or on the front line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: (redacted) (redacted) . After the attack, when we were taken to the house where Pole took the weapons away from us, the weapons we had with us. That night I spent in the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So you persist in saying that you were in the house.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the course of the operations, I was in the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: We will not pursue the matter. Tell me: All those other 75 men that you mentioned here were armed, were they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they were not. Because there were also old people and women and those younger ones who were detained with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Just a moment. I'm following up on your statement. 75 men, all men who were arrested were members of the TO. I'm asking you about your statement. That is what you stated. 75 men, members of the territorial defence, were they all armed? I'm asking you again.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You mean they were TO members but had no weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, some did have their weapons, but they handed down their weapons that evening when we were made to go to Stipo Pole's house. But we were not all armed. There were very few weapons there. Those who were arrested later, they were the ones who had weapons on them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, please, perhaps you hid your weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot hide a weapon, because I handed it over. I was issued a receipt, and I have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, please, was there a trench around your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And your brothers, were they members of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, wasn't a huge amount of ammunition, automatic rifles, found near your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there was never at my place.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: In your hamlet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W [Resumed]
